newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The opposition will challenge the government's ability to balance the budget for fiscal 1998 and accuse it of seeking to embark on a spending spree during the budget bill debate today. The government, desperate to generate income and having already cut deep into this year's spending, will be hard-pressed to balance the budget amid grim economic conditions. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The victim in the Taurus pub shooting case has met with police and reversed his original statement in which he accuses the son of a business tycoon of attempting to kill him during a brawl. Police Maj Gen Jongrak Juthanond, who is overseeing the case, says the victim has told him that Suksan Kongudom, son of Chatchawal Kongudom, did not attack him or engage in the shooting that seriously wounded him. (THE NATION) (BANGKOK POST)

- The police chief has turned down the offer of a position at the Royal Sports Club and Royal Turf Club. Police Gen Pracha Promnok is understood to have declined the offer of an honorary executive title because it is thought to have been intended to halt police operations against illegal bookmakers. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Cabinet has approved four Royal decrees, including one which allows greater foreign equity participation in banks and finance companies. The decrees are aimed at encouraging mergers among financial institutions and contain provisions to allow securitization of finance firm loans to help the troubled property sector. (BUSINESS DAY)

- The Industry Ministry will next month finalise a 10 billion baht Thailand-Japan joint investment to establish a fishery complex in Samut Sakhon province. There will be a meeting between Thai and Japanese investors on July 18 when agreement on details of the planned fishing industrial estate project is expected. (THE NATION)
